scope.definition: Observability-to-remediation is the closed loop from telemetry/event detection through correlation, diagnosis, action selection, execution, verification, rollback/escalation, and learning. It includes error-centric Sentry/Seer, AIOps correlation assistants, deterministic runbook engines, Kubernetes reconcilers and progressive-delivery rollback. It excludes generic coding agents except when handed an incident-derived diagnosis and excludes mere dashboards/notifications.
scope.covered_signals: Errors/stack traces, logs, metrics/SLOs, distributed traces, profiles, release/deployment metadata, topology/change events, incident records and repository/test context [S01,S02,S04,S05,S28].
autonomy_levels: L2 human-triggered vetted runbook or patch draft
L3 policy-triggered bounded runbook with automatic verification/rollback
L4 agent invents and deploys a novel repair without approval
scope.evidence_boundary: As of 2026-09-13, L1-L2 are broadly productized; narrow L3 is mature for predefined reversible actions and desired-state reconciliation; general L4 is not supported by credible reliability evidence [S09,S35,S37,S42,S45,S49].

current_state: Verified: Sentry Seer can consume issue telemetry plus linked source, produce RCA, plan and code, and open a draft PR/MR or hand off to coding agents. Admins cap automation at RCA, plan, or PR draft. Documentation does not describe auto-merge/deploy [S02,S26].

Verified: PagerDuty, Dynatrace, Datadog and AWS-style stacks connect anomaly/incident context to approved actions or pre-authored runbooks. Their diagnosis and actuation layers must be distinguished: ML/LLM suggestions do not by themselves make execution safe [S09,S10,S12,S35,S36,S38,S39,S42].

Verified: Kubernetes controllers/probes and Argo Rollouts already implement useful closed loops: converge desired state, restart unhealthy containers, pause/abort/rollback deployments based on metric predicates [S07,S08,S24,S45,S46].

Independent benchmark evidence is much weaker than product breadth. ITBench's best tested model achieved 13.81% diagnosis and 11.43% mitigation pass@1 on its SRE scenarios and 0% on hard repair; traces materially helped. Therefore novel end-to-end remediation remains experimental [S49].

Inference: the most production-ready architecture is hybrid: probabilistic systems rank evidence/propose; deterministic policy and reviewed runbooks actuate; CI/canary/postconditions decide promotion or rollback [S13,S32,S35,S39,S49].

primary_evidence: Sentry's current docs explicitly specify data inputs, three-stage collaboration, SCM scope, automation thresholds/stopping points, diff/PR review and optional checks. This verifies mechanics, not model correctness [S01,S02,S03,S27,S28].

Open standards/project docs verify signal correlation and actuator primitives: W3C Trace Context; OpenTelemetry signal/status/resiliency; Prometheus webhook; Kubernetes controllers/probes; Argo analysis/rollback [S04-S08,S24,S43-S46].

Vendor docs consistently expose approvals and scope controls rather than unrestricted autonomy: Datadog Ask/Deny guardrails, Dynatrace approval timeout, PagerDuty pre-created actions, and SSM aws:approve [S35,S37,S39,S42].

Incident postmortems demonstrate mechanism-level hazards: global rollout, excessive capacity removal, shared-fate safety checker failure, fallback/blocklist positive feedback, and control-plane impairment [S16,S17,S29-S31].
independent_evidence: ITBench is the closest live, tool-using, multi-signal evaluation. It finds observability useful but low absolute diagnosis/mitigation reliability and 0% hard repairs; injected Kubernetes incidents still underrepresent organic production complexity [S49].
AIOpsLab supplies an end-to-end evaluation design, but its published prototype result is one case and cannot establish production readiness [S50].
Peer-reviewed cloud-incident work supports historical-incident retrieval and RCA/mitigation recommendation, not safe autonomous execution [S51].

APR and repository benchmarks show test-oracle and contamination problems: test-passing can be wrong; SWE-bench's container score omits rollout, security and blast radius; SWE-Bench+ reports leakage/weak-test inflation [S19,S20,S22,S34,S52].

Independent public evidence specifically auditing Sentry's 94.5% RCA claim, Datadog/Dynatrace agentic actions, or customer MTTR/false-action distributions was not found. Vendor case studies are reported separately [S26,S29,S40].

reference_workflow: 1. Instrument: emit structured logs, metrics, traces/profiles and release/change IDs through OpenTelemetry; propagate W3C trace IDs; redact secrets/PII at source. Track collector drop/queue health because missing telemetry is an unsafe input [S03-S05,S43,S44].

2. Detect: evaluate user-impact/SLO symptoms with persistence (`for`), hysteresis and missing-data rules. Group/deduplicate alerts; attach service, environment, version, owner, trace IDs and stable incident/action ID [S06,S14].
3. Enrich: join recent deploy/commit/config/feature-flag and topology/dependency data; retrieve similar resolved incidents and approved runbooks. Preserve raw evidence and provenance [S28,S36,S51].

4. Triage: deterministic rules first suppress duplicates and classify known signatures. A probabilistic RCA assistant may rank hypotheses with citations and uncertainty. It must not silently convert correlation to cause [S35,S38,S49].

5. Choose autonomy: match an allowlisted known condition to a versioned idempotent runbook. Unknown/ambiguous cases create incident + diagnostic bundle. Code defects may enter Sentry RCA→editable plan→patch branch/draft PR, never direct default-branch mutation [S02,S09,S39,S47].

6. Preflight: acquire per-resource lock; dedupe by incident/action ID; verify preconditions, maintenance/freeze window, current desired state, error-budget/blast-radius budget, recent actions, backups and rollback feasibility. Simulate/dry-run where supported [S07,S13,S32].

7. Gate: auto-execute only low-risk reversible actions (restart one replica, scale within bounds, fail over a canary, toggle a pre-approved flag). Require named approval/quorum for destructive, stateful, multi-region, permission, schema or novel code changes [S35,S37,S42].

8. Execute: use short-lived least-privilege identity in an isolated runner. Canary one cell/tenant/replica first; bound concurrency, retries, rate and total affected resources; maintain an out-of-band kill switch [S16,S17,S30-S32].

9. Verify: compare canary/control and independent user-impact SLO plus technical postconditions over a fixed observation window. Do not treat alert disappearance alone as success. Record action output and telemetry completeness [S07,S29,S32,S52].
10. Commit or compensate: promote gradually only if all invariants pass. Otherwise stop, roll back/execute compensating action, inhibit repeated retries and page a human with evidence [S07,S24,S47].

11. Learn: append immutable incident/action/outcome record; link reviewed fix, tests and postmortem; convert only repeatedly successful repairs into candidate allowlisted runbooks through review. Measure recurrence and false-action harm, not just MTTR [S23,S33].
integration_points: Telemetry: OpenTelemetry APIs/SDKs/Collector/OTLP; W3C trace context; Sentry SDK/error/log/trace/profile ingestion; Prometheus-compatible metrics [S01,S04,S05,S43,S44].
Detection/routing: Sentry issue/metric alerts and webhooks; Prometheus rules→Alertmanager webhook; PagerDuty Events/Event Orchestration; CloudWatch/EventBridge [S06,S38,S39].
Context: service catalog/CMDB, ownership/on-call, deployment/release/commit metadata, feature flags, Kubernetes events/topology, incident history and runbook registry [S28,S36,S51].

Actuation: SSM Automation, PagerDuty Automation Actions, Dynatrace Workflows, Datadog Private Action Runner, StackStorm/Rundeck, Kubernetes API/Operators and Argo Rollouts [S09,S10,S24,S35,S42,S45-S47].
Code path: Sentry↔GitHub.com/GitLab.com repos; branch/draft PR/MR; optional coding-agent handoff; CI tests, security/static checks and required owner review before merge [S02,S27].

State/audit: durable queue plus dedupe ledger, workflow state machine, action/checkpoint/artifact store, append-only audit and incident timeline. Alertmanager webhook alone is not a durable exactly-once job system; idempotency is required because retries/replays are possible [S06].
Feedback: deployment event closes loop into release health/SLO dashboards; incident tracker/postmortem and private replay suite supply outcome labels [S23,S28,S33].
human_gates: Always approve novel code, database/schema/data-destructive changes, security/IAM changes, cross-region/global actions, customer communication and actions without a proven compensator. Reason: correctness and blast radius are not established by RCA confidence [S15-S17,S49].

Sentry's recommended boundary is concrete: admins cap at RCA/plan/PR draft; users edit plans/diffs; nothing merges without approval. Keep third-party AI review optional rather than a single availability-dependent required check [S02,S26,S27].
Use explicit approval objects with named roles, quorum and timeout. Dynatrace declines/24h timeout fail the workflow; SSM `aws:approve` pauses for selected principals [S37,S42].

Auto-run only high-frequency known signatures with a stable deterministic runbook, low bounded impact, recent successful drills, verified rollback and healthy observability. Escalate on ambiguity, missing signals, budget exhaustion, conflicting hypotheses, repeated attempt or verification failure [S09,S32,S44,S47].
A human incident commander retains kill-switch authority and validates business/user impact. The agent may gather evidence and draft updates, but generated claims require fact checking [S23,S29].
failure_modes: Bad/stale/missing telemetry, sampling or collector drops causes false negatives and wrong RCA; trace context may be broken across queues/services [S04,S05,S44,S49].
Correlation is mistaken for causation; model hallucinates a command, file, dependency or confident RCA; similar-incident retrieval imports obsolete context [S26,S49,S51].
Test/verification oracle is weak: patch clears a narrow test/alert while violating semantics, security, latency, data integrity or downstream behavior [S20,S22,S34,S52].
Automation amplification: global rollout, unbounded capacity removal, blocklist/fallback cascade, retries/thundering herd or shared-fate safety checker expands blast radius [S16,S17,S29-S31].
Non-idempotent webhook retry or duplicate alert repeats a destructive action; concurrent workflows fight; stale desired state causes oscillation/flapping [S06,S45,S47].

Rollback is unavailable or unsafe after schema migration, irreversible external effect, cache/protocol incompatibility or data corruption; control plane/auth/DNS is impaired by the incident [S17,S24].

Permissions are too broad; telemetry/repo contains secrets or prompt injection; agent exfiltrates code/data or changes its own controls; subprocessor/data-residency boundary is unacceptable [S03,S35,S37].

Economic/organizational: noisy triggers, LLM/tool latency and token/telemetry cost, vendor lock-in, workflow drift, abandoned projects (Keptn), missing runbook ownership and automation complacency [S13,S41,S48].

Evaluation failure: vendor metric lacks denominator; public benchmark is contaminated or not representative; injected faults omit organic socio-technical incidents and long-horizon recurrence [S19,S20,S26,S34,S49].
controls_and_mitigations: Identity/data: per-service least privilege, short-lived credentials, network egress allowlist, repo/environment scoping, secret/PII redaction, immutable audit, separation of proposer/approver/executor [S03,S35,S37,S42].
Trigger quality: SLO/symptom alerts, debounce/hysteresis, maintenance suppression, dedupe/inhibition, minimum evidence and explicit unknown/missing-data state [S06,S14,S44].

Action safety: signed/versioned allowlist; schema-validated parameters; pre/postconditions; idempotency key and resource lock; max attempts/concurrency/rate/affected resources/cost; cool-down; never let agent edit its policy [S15,S30,S45,S47].

Blast radius: shadow mode, dry run, single-cell canary, gradual promotion, objective canary/control analysis, protected baseline capacity, circuit breaker and out-of-band kill switch [S07,S16,S17,S29,S32].

Validation: reproduce in isolated environment; regression/security/static tests; independent SLO and user journey; observation window; require multiple signals for high-risk actions. A passed repository test or cleared alert is insufficient [S20,S34,S49,S52].
Recovery: precompute compensator/rollback, verify backup restore and break-glass channel, stop retries on failed verification, preserve evidence and page human [S17,S23,S24].

Governance: named owner/expiry for every runbook; two-person review for scope increases; quarterly incident replays/chaos drills; action outcome labels; kill or narrow automations with rising false-action/rollback rate [S13,S23,S33].

maturity_assessment.production_ready: Signal collection/correlation primitives; actionable alert routing; desired-state Kubernetes reconciliation; health restart; progressive delivery abort/rollback; human-triggered or policy-triggered vetted runbooks for low-risk reversible cases [S04-S10,S24,S43-S47].
maturity_assessment.emerging: AI multi-signal RCA, plan generation, patch drafts and agentic recommendations. Sentry core is GA but relies on approval; Datadog remediation and Dynatrace agentic actions are Preview [S02,S26,S35,S36].
maturity_assessment.experimental: Model chooses and safely executes a novel repair or code deployment across heterogeneous production without human review. ITBench's low pass@1 and 0% hard repair contradict readiness [S49].
maturity_assessment.rationale: The actuator technology is mature; diagnosis validity, test oracles, permissions and blast-radius control are the bottleneck. Production postmortems show deterministic automation can itself be the incident [S15-S17,S29-S31].

build_vs_buy.buy: Buy observability/AIOps UI, telemetry retention/correlation, on-call workflow and common integrations when they match existing stack: Sentry for application errors/code context; Datadog/Dynatrace for unified telemetry; PagerDuty for incident/runbook orchestration [S01,S09-S11,S35-S39].
build_vs_buy.build_or_own: Own the safety/control plane even with SaaS: event schema, durable queue/dedupe ledger, service/runbook catalog, permissions, risk classifier, approval policy, canary/postcondition checks, compensators, audit and private replay evaluation. These encode local architecture and business invariants no vendor can infer reliably [S29,S32,S49].
build_vs_buy.open_source: OpenTelemetry + Prometheus/Alertmanager + Kubernetes Operators/Argo Rollouts + StackStorm/Rundeck gives portability and inspectability but transfers HA, upgrades, connector security and runbook maintenance to the team [S04,S06,S07,S43-S47].
build_vs_buy.avoid: Do not base a greenfield control plane on AWS Incident Manager (closed to new customers) or archived Keptn without explicit lifecycle risk acceptance [S41,S48].

recommended_pattern.lane_A: Known-condition lane: deterministic match→versioned low-risk runbook→bounded canary→independent verify→gradual commit or automatic compensate. It may be fully closed loop only inside an explicit autonomy envelope.
recommended_pattern.lane_B: Unknown/code lane: AI assembles evidence and ranked hypotheses→human confirms RCA/plan→sandbox patch→CI/security/replay→draft PR→owner approval→progressive delivery→automatic rollback on SLO breach.
recommended_pattern.initial_rollout: Start shadow-only and replay the last 20–50 incidents. Then enable read-only diagnostics. Next enable human-click runbooks. Auto-run only a handful of reversible actions after severity-stratified trials show acceptable false-action and rollback rates. Expand per service, not globally [S32,S49].
recommended_pattern.minimum_metrics: Detection precision/recall; RCA top-k calibration; action attempt/success; false-action and rollback rate; time to detect bad action; affected-user minutes; recurrence within 7/30 days; telemetry completeness; cost per incident; human override; change failure and recovery time [S33,S49].
recommended_pattern.decision_rule: Optimize user harm and recurrence, not number of auto-fixes or headline MTTR. If telemetry is incomplete, verification disagrees, or rollback is uncertain, fail closed and escalate.

open_questions: What are severity-stratified false-positive RCA and harmful-action rates on recent private incidents, including no-action incidents? Public vendor figures do not answer this [S26,S49].
How should RCA confidence be calibrated across model/version/tool changes, and what threshold maps to each autonomy envelope?
Can the organization build a faithful replay/sandbox for stateful, multi-region, security and partial-control-plane incidents without leaking production secrets?
Which actions have truly reversible compensators after schema/data/external side effects, and how often are rollback paths drilled [S17,S24]?
How will telemetry provenance and completeness be proved when Collector queues drop data or tracing is sampled/broken [S44]?
How are prompt injection and untrusted logs/issues/code isolated from tools with write credentials [S03]?
What are full costs: telemetry retention, model tokens, action runners, false pages, workflow ownership and vendor add-ons?
Will Preview surfaces (Datadog Bits Remediation, Dynatrace agentic Intelligence) retain APIs/controls and meet compliance/SLA needs [S35,S36]?
What replacement path is available for AWS Incident Manager greenfield users and for archived Keptn deployments [S41,S48]?

confidence.overall: High for architecture/mechanics and maturity classification; medium for comparative product performance; low for vendor outcome metrics.
confidence.high: Official current docs establish integration, gate and status mechanics [S01-S12,S24,S35-S48]. Standards and regulator/postmortem evidence strongly establish control principles [S05,S13-S17,S23,S29-S33].
confidence.medium: Academic live benchmarks support the conclusion that novel remediation is unreliable, but scenario/model coverage and production realism are limited [S49,S50].
confidence.low: Sentry accuracy/time-saved and Ryanair savings lack independent protocol/audit [S26,S40]. No defensible cross-vendor MTTR or total-cost ranking was found.
confidence.claim_policy: Statements labeled vendor claim/case study are not treated as independent validation; inferences are explicitly marked and grounded in cited mechanisms.

conflicts: Vendor framing versus operational boundary: products use 'autonomous/agentic/remediation' language, while docs require click/approval or stop at draft PR and mark important action surfaces Preview [S02,S35-S37]. Likely cause: autonomy refers to subtasks, not authority to merge/deploy.

Sentry reports 94.5% RCA accuracy [S26], while ITBench's best tested live-agent diagnosis pass@1 is 13.81% [S49]. These are not comparable: proprietary traffic/labels and undisclosed exclusions versus adversarial reproducible scenarios. Prefer neither as universal; require local replay.

Repository-repair scores appear to improve, but SWE-Bench+ finds leakage and weak-test inflation and SWE-bench evaluation omits rollout safety [S20,S34]. Likely cause: benchmark/task/test selection and model knowledge contamination.

Automation improves consistency [S13] but postmortems show it replicates mistakes rapidly [S15-S17,S29-S31]. Resolution: restrict closed loop to convergent/reversible actions with independent invariants and small blast radius.

Sentry's own incident shows AI can localize an automation cascade while the cascade itself came from flawed automatic protection [S29]. This supports collaborative diagnosis, not a claim that adding AI makes automation safe.
uncertain: No independently audited production distribution for Sentry Seer RCA correctness, patch acceptance, regression rate, deployment outcomes or severity mix was located.
No apples-to-apples independent benchmark across Sentry, Datadog, Dynatrace, PagerDuty and cloud-native compositions was located.
Preview/GA labels and commercial tier details can change after 2026-09-13; current docs were used where available.
ITBench is the best located end-to-end evidence but remains injected Kubernetes scenarios and may not predict organic multi-team incidents.
Source S52 DOI/title metadata is used only for its well-known 2/105 patch-correctness result; readers should verify publisher metadata during formal bibliography production.
Costs, latency, regional data residency and availability SLAs are workload/contract specific and could not be normalized from public sources.
The future of Shoreline functionality after its redirect/acquisition path was not sufficiently documented, so it was excluded from recommendations.
